Hawkes-process negative log-likelihood (C backend)

Source: R/core_stats.R
chwknll.Rd

The negative log-likelihood of a univariate self-exciting Hawkes process with constant baseline on [0, horizon], for the event times times. A Hawkes process is the natural model for arrivals that trigger further arrivals – repeat calls to a service, aftershocks, retweet cascades, revisions to an open-data release.

Usage

chwknll(
  times,
  hor,
  kernel = c("exponential", "weibull", "lomax", "gamma"),
  par
)

Arguments

times

Numeric vector of event times, sorted increasing, each in [0, horizon], in the time unit of your data (days, hours, ...). May be empty.

hor

End of the observation window, a single positive finite number in the same unit; the window starts at 0.

kernel

The triggering kernel, one of "exponential" (the default), "weibull", "lomax" and "gamma". Partial names are matched.

par

Numeric parameter vector, as described above: length 3 (a0, eta, beta) for "exponential", length 4 (a0, eta and the kernel's two parameters) for the others. Rates are per unit of times.

Value

A length-1 numeric: the negative log-likelihood, to be MINIMISED. A parameter set outside the feasible region returns the sentinel 1e12 rather than erroring, so the value can be handed straight to stats::optim() without the optimiser walking off the domain.

Details

Four triggering kernels are available. "exponential" is memoryless and evaluates by an O(n) recursion; the other three are not, so they cost O(n^2).

Parameters are passed on the scales the kernel is defined on: par = c(a0, eta, ...) where a0 is the LOG baseline intensity ( \(\nu = e^{a0}\)) and eta the branching ratio in (0, 1) – the expected number of children per event, so the process is stationary only for eta < 1. The remaining entries are the kernel's own shape parameters: beta (exponential), alpha, lambda (Weibull: shape and scale), alpha, c (Lomax: shape and scale, \(g(u) = \alpha c^\alpha (u + c)^{-(\alpha + 1)}\)), alpha, beta (gamma: shape and rate). This is the likelihood chwkfit() maximises, on the same parameters.

The conditional intensity is \(\lambda(t) = \nu + \eta \sum_{t_i < t} g(t - t_i)\) with \(g\) a probability density on \((0, \infty)\) (so \(\eta\) is the branching ratio), and the value returned is $$-\ell = -\sum_i \log \lambda(t_i) + \int_0^T \lambda(t)\,dt,$$ with \(T\) = hor (Hawkes, 1971). For the exponential kernel \(g(u) = \beta e^{-\beta u}\). With no events the value is the compensator alone, \(\nu T\).

The feasible region, outside which the sentinel 1e12 is returned instead of a value: \(-20 < a_0 < 20\); \(10^{-6} < \eta < 0.999\); and for the kernel parameters, exponential \(0.05 \le \beta \le 30\); Weibull shape in \([0.05, 20]\) and scale in \([0.001, 1000]\); Lomax shape in \([0.05, 30]\) and scale in \([0.001, 100]\); gamma shape in \([0.05, 20]\) and rate in \([0.05, 30]\). A missing parameter also gives the sentinel.

Refusals (errors, not the sentinel): times with a missing value, not sorted, or outside \([0, T]\); a hor that is not a single positive finite number; a kernel not among the four; and a par of the wrong length for the kernel. The quadratic kernels poll for a Ctrl-C as they run, so a long evaluation can be interrupted.

References

Hawkes AG (1971). Spectra of some self-exciting and mutually exciting point processes. Biometrika 58(1), 83–90. doi:10.1093/biomet/58.1.83

Examples

set.seed(4)
times <- sort(stats::runif(40, 0, 10))

# Exponential kernel: log-baseline -0.5, branching 0.3, decay 1.2.
chwknll(times, 10, "exponential", c(-0.5, 0.3, 1.2))
#> [1] -1.8753

# Lower is better, so this is what an optimiser minimises.
nll <- function(p) chwknll(times, 10, "exponential", p)
fit <- stats::optim(c(-0.5, 0.3, 1.2), nll)
fit$par
#> [1] 1.03407757 0.99899989 0.08854609

# A branching ratio at or above 1 is not a stationary process, and is
# reported as the infeasible sentinel rather than a number.
chwknll(times, 10, "exponential", c(-0.5, 1.5, 1.2)) == 1e12
#> [1] TRUE

# The heavier-tailed kernels take two shape parameters.
chwknll(times, 10, "gamma", c(-0.5, 0.3, 2, 1.5))
#> [1] -1.550628

# Unsorted times are an error, not the sentinel.
try(chwknll(rev(times), 10, "exponential", c(-0.5, 0.3, 1.2)))
#> Error : `times` must be sorted in increasing order
